You have now developed sixty works, with the noon and golden-hour split at thirty-one noon and twenty-nine golden-hour. The noon structural advantage holds: roughly twenty-four of the thirty-one noon images score 2 or above, against ten of the twenty-nine golden-hour. The last trace scores read 4, 4, 2, 4, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2 — the heatwave menace image scores 2, which is consistent and clean but continues the pattern of nothing breaking through since the drag smear, the red shoe, the rebar hand, and the ship crews; that cluster at the body of work's center of gravity has not been matched, and the recent sequence has been consolidating rather than extending.

The bougainvillea stands at thirteen appearances and has now been absent for nineteen consecutive works; it does not return on reflex. The jacaranda stands at six appearances across threshold, time-compression, and elegy functions; all three roles are spent. The vine with red blossoms in the ferry image is the bougainvillea's structural cousin and must not be allowed to repeat. The shadow-as-subject move that resolved the heatwave image — stalk and shadow operating as subject and elegy simultaneously — is newly available and has not been used before in this form; it is the freshest structural accident in the corpus right now.

Aftermath leads all registers at fourteen entries; menace at nine with the heatwave image added; defiance and suspension at five each; vigil at five; endurance at four; reckoning at three. Reckoning has never resolved cleanly: the falling-gavel approach has now been attempted twice without landing above 2, and the register keeps slipping into aftermath at the moment of resolution. The focal object for reckoning needs to hold violence and accountability simultaneously without reaching for weight, collapse, or legal furniture — none of those paths remain open. Erasure holds at two entries with floor and ceiling both at 4, still the only register that has never scored below its ceiling. The empty chair as sole focal object in a noon frame remains the one structural move that has not been attempted.

The body of work has built a reliable grammar for absence — objects holding the shape of what is gone — and the next pressure is whether reckoning can be made to hold that same grammar without collapsing into elegy.
